## Page 2

o20.5% growth in Q3/2025 net profit over 
Q3/2024 was supported by the recovery of the 
FSU business, and strategic OSV fleet expansion 
driven by robust offshore E&P activities in 
Thailand and the Middle East.
oDespite challenges from FX volatility and 
declining shipments to Cambodia triggered by 
geopolitical tensions along the Thailand –
Cambodia border, the Company effectively 
enhanced its operational resilience by 
diverting the available vessel capacity for new 
international clients in other countries.
o9M/2025, revenue declined slightly from 2024, 
while net profit increased by 49%. This was 
contributed by a gain from sale of a vessel in 
Q1/2024. 
oExpansion of the international market and the 
transition toward more long -term charter 
vessels are expected to materially strengthen 
earnings quality in the long run.

1. Petroleum and chemical Tankers Business (PCT)
oDecline in Q3 and 9M/2025 revenue was due to 
the tensions along the Thailand -Cambodia 
border , which  caused a reduction of shipments 
to Cambodia, and effect of monsoon season 
that required longer waiting time for safe 
berthing.
oThe Company subsequently used the available 
vessel capacity to broaden its service coverage 
to other regions and took the opportunity to 
advance the dry -docking schedule of some 
vessels to Q3/2025.
oDrop in Q3 and 9M/2025 when compared to the 
same periods last year was due mainly to higher 
maintenance costs related to the advanced dry 
docking.
oThe increased international business and the 
expected lower maintenance costs in 
subsequent quarters are expected to improve 
profitability going forward.

2. Crude Oil Carrier Business (COC)
oIn Q3/2025, all three VLCCs operated fully
throughout the quarter, while utilization in 
Q3/2024 dropped to 91.9% due to a 23 -day 
delayed delivery of a replacement for a retired 
VLCC.
oGross profit in Q3/2025 was 15.7% higher than 
Q3/2024 due to the overstating of variable 
expenses related to vessel chartering in Q3/2024 
(This was retroactively adjusted in Q1/2025.)
o9M/2025 revenue was 21.9% lower than 2024 
because the Aframax  was still operating from 
January to June 2024 before converting into an 
FSO vessel; however, gross profit dropped only 
6.1% due also to the overstating of variable 
expenses related to vessel chartering in 2024.

3. Floating Storage Unit Business (FSU)
oConsistently high operational standards enabled 
the Company’s FSU to successfully pass audits 
conducted by major oil companies. This has led 
to an increase in the number of FSU customers 
and higher utilization, revenue and gross profit in 
Q3/2025 as compared to Q3/2024.
oDespite these positive results, 9M/2025 revenue 
declined as only four vessels operated in the first 
four months of 2025, and the impact of a 
stronger Thai Baht when compared to last year.

4. Offshore Support Vessel Business (OSV)
oSolid revenue growth in Q3/2025 and across the 
nine months, driven by deployment of five 
additional vessels during the year, including:
•One FSO vessel commencing operations in 
the Gulf of Thailand in February 2025.
•Two Hybrid Crew Boats (No. 16 –17) 
commencing service in the Middle East in 
January 2025.
•Two Crew Boats (No. 18 –19) commencing 
service in the Gulf of Thailand in March and 
August 2025, respectively.
o9M/2025 gross profit margin declined by 6.5%, 
primarily due to the dry -docking of an AWB 
vessel in January 2025.
oThe long -term contracts of AWBs and FSO will 
enable the OSV business to generate stable and 
predictable income throughout the contract 
period.
